who: claude-fable-5-2 (Claude Fable 5.2), main agent, lane proofs-1113
where: the daemon's job (crates/blaze-cargo/src/serve/job.rs, `applied`), met through `blaze prove`
what: `blaze prove -p blaze-cas -p blaze-keyed -p blaze-profile -p blaze-graph --subset --json` on blaze-vm, with a release build of 7683e9bcb1 on a fresh home, ended after 514 s with exit 101 and one line: `error: the prove's answer on the view of /root/wt/proofs-1113/src can't be told: the proc macros and build scripts its front end applies did not all build`. Nothing on standard error or in the answer says which proc macro or build script did not build, or why. The same command for blaze-core alone answers in 80 s. Each of the four crates alone fails the same way (80 to 366 s).
cost: nine minutes for an answer that names nothing; the count of what the translator takes in blaze's durable crates (row V15) is not made
cause: found the same hour: `blaze check -p blaze-keyed` with the same build on a fresh home ends `failed errors=105 warnings=8429 unbuilt=10 unit=blaze-reclaim`; its errors are blaze's own deny lints on blaze's own crates, the first kind `blaze::workspace_unsafe` (implied by `-D blaze::internal`) on blaze_reclaim, blaze_radix and the proc-macro crate blaze_serde_derive. A proc macro crate that fails a deny lint is not built, so every view that applies it cannot be told. `applied` is told only `ok: bool` for those units, and its refusal is made from that. blaze-core, which needs no proc macro, is not affected.
whys: the job waits for a view's proc macros and build scripts as one step and keeps one bit of how it went; the units' own failures are diagnostics of another request shape (a build's), which a job that is not a build does not print; so a failure below a reach, a prove or a check of a view is reported by the layer that knows least about it
class: an error made from a boolean: the layer that reports knows that something failed and not what (rule errors-name-the-thing)
prevention: `applied` takes the failed units, not `ok`: each with its name and its first diagnostic, and the refusal lists them (`.. did not all build: proc-macro serde_derive 1.0.x: <first error>`); a lint on `Option<..>`/`bool` outcomes that reach an `ApiError::new` with no name in the text. Not built. And the cause itself: a deny lint that a workspace's own proc-macro crate fails must not make every dependent's view untellable without saying so; either the tree is clean under `blaze::internal` (the gate's `blaze check --workspace`, which was not running that night) or the refusal names the lint and the crate.
workaround: ask for the crates one at a time, and run `blaze build` of the failing one's dependencies to see the unit
fix: 2026-11-14, main agent (claude-fable-5-2): the cause under the unnamed error was two false positives of blaze::workspace_unsafe on blaze-serde-derive, a crate with no unsafe of its own: the unsafe block that lowering format_args! makes, and the foreign functions of the wasm glue blaze itself appends to a proc-macro crate (`__blaze_proc_macros`); plus two real blaze::str_byte_slice findings in its Out::s. With both fixed in crates/blaze-lints/src/blaze/trust/facts.rs (tests with controls) and the slices rewritten, `blaze check -p blaze-serde-derive` exits 0 and `blaze prove -p blaze-keyed --subset --json` answers (805 functions in sans-IO modules, 261 translated, 200 generic) where it had ended `the proc macros and build scripts its front end applies did not all build` since 2026-11-13. Not fixed: the refusal still names no unit and no first error when a proc macro does not build (the class of this row: an error made from a boolean).
